title: to_ipv6 maps bool to loopback (::1/::)
description:
## Problem

python/src/lichen/ipv6/addr.py to_ipv6() is the routing-table canonicalizer (loadng RouteCache, GradientTable, RPL paths, gateway handoff). It documents AddrError for any invalid input and accepts only IPv6Address, str, or 16 packed bytes.

Because ipaddress.IPv6Address treats bool as int:
- to_ipv6(True) -> ::1 (loopback)
- to_ipv6(False) -> ::

Verified with the stdlib constructor. Sibling helpers in the same file already reject bool via type(x) is int (unicast_prefix_based_mcast group_id, _normalize_zone_id).

## Why it matters

A JSON/CBOR boolean in an address field does not fail closed. Traffic or a route cache entry is bound to loopback instead of being rejected. That is silent misdelivery at a system boundary.

## Where

python/src/lichen/ipv6/addr.py:30-47 (to_ipv6)
Callers: python/src/lichen/loadng/cache.py, python/src/lichen/gradient.py, python/src/lichen/rpl/routing.py, python/src/lichen/gateway/handoff.py
design: Reject bool explicitly (bool is an int subclass). Do not accept arbitrary ints unless the documented contract is expanded; the current docstring allows only IPv6Address, str, and 16-byte packed data.
acceptance_criteria: to_ipv6(True) and to_ipv6(False) raise AddrError. to_ipv6 still accepts IPv6Address, str, and 16-byte packed values. Tests cover the bool rejection without weakening existing vector checks. loadng/gradient/rpl call sites keep using to_ipv6 as the coercer.
close_reason: to_ipv6 rejects bool/int (stdlib maps True/False to ::1/::). Tests cover bool rejection plus documented IPv6Address/str/packed-bytes forms. loadng/gradient/rpl still coerce via to_ipv6.
